reviewMethod: Read both complete harness files and retained actual Chromium output, verify all fifteen current source/test hashes and asserted outcomes. No browser/test rerun by reviewer.
acceptedBehavior: The actual hook decodes synthetic image bytes, reads the real raster and calls the production detector. Only OCR boundary responses and the counted legacy-reader boundary are controlled.
Two real OriginalChartEvidence consumers share one owning hook. Deferred evidence is held; completed real pure-verifier evidence produces exact expected original-pixel SVG endpoints in both views.
The SVG y coordinates reflect projected candidate prices, not the deliberately bad raw model y. Changes in candidate price change measured SVG y from 202.5 to 143.5 in the fixture.

Revocation synchronously removes lines; reconfirmation and changed confirmation object require fresh evidence. Late old-report, A-B-A, and revoked/reconfirmed callbacks that ignore abort do not resurrect geometry.

Even valid model bounds with false model quality cannot gain legacy candle/axis authority from recovery. Pattern/liquidity SVGs remain absent and the legacy reader is never invoked across all scenarios.
Explicit log scale, malformed limitations/candidates, touching-panel ambiguity and over-budget images hold before new OCR; the oversized new-only path also holds before raster readback.

Explicit OCR hold, rejected reader, nonlinear numeric evidence and a bare forged verified envelope all hold. Shared consumer removal does not restart OCR or loop renders; unmount aborts and ignores late completion.

Runner permits only local origin/data requests, closes browser/server in finally, records failures and exits unsuccessfully if a scenario fails. No silent browser fallback or external/provider access is present.
scopeLimits: The production browser-image-axis-ocr wrapper is mocked by this lifecycle harness. Its actual source is covered separately by four controlled adapter cases and strict TypeScript; neither is real recognition accuracy proof.

This harness uses public synthetic PNG rasters. It reads no private original, oracle or held-out case. It does not establish retained d001 OCR, the one-pixel benchmark, semantic support/resistance correctness or generalization.
Local Chromium and source hashes are verified; complete-tree hosted TS/build/affected gates and actual retained OCR remain separate pending evidence.
Desktop headless lifecycle checks are not physical-device responsiveness measurements.
